newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Friday on uncertainties over the short-term market trend, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at 3,205 yuan ($386) per tonne, losing 30 yuan. It opened at 3,206 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 3,234 and a low of 3,194.
March was unchanged at 3,230, May rose eight to 3,340, July fell two to 3,378, September dropped one to 3,388 and November rose two to 3,401.
Combined volume rose to 16,300 tonnes from 10,000.
Traders said most investors stayed on the sidelines with the short-term market trend remaining unclear.
"Investors were still taking a wait-and-see attitude given no market-moving news," one trader said.
"The whole market seemed to be asleep for most of the session," he added.
Traders expect soybean to move around 3,200 yuan in the next few days.
